title: Explore genetic and genomic associations for lupus
bodyHtml:
This page allows you to explore results relevant to the genetic architecture of systemic lupus erythematosus, from an analysis of 7,219 European-ancestry SLE cases and 15,991 controls (Bentham, Morris, et al., 2015). Visit the Signal Sifter to view lupus-associated variants in a genomic region of interest in the context of thousands of tissue-specific genomic annotations.

  • Click on the "camera" icon at the upper right of each section to prepare the data in that section for downloading. Then click on the "Data files" icon at the upper right of this page to see the list of the data files you requested and download them in .csv and/or JSON format.
  • Click on the "eye" icon at the upper right of each section to hide or show that section.
  • Click on a column header in the tables below to sort the table by that column.
The table below displays genome-wide significant associations (p ≤ 5e-8) from this study. 
Top common variant gene-level associations (p-value ≤ 0.05) from this study, as determined by the MAGMA method. Mouse over the plot to see gene names and p-values. 
Top pathways enriched for genes associated with SLE (p-value ≤ 0.05), as determined by the MAGMA method. 
Phenotypes genetically correlated with SLE, as determined by cross-trait LD score regression. Genetic associations are drawn from the Association to Function Knowledge Portal (A2FKP). 

Tissue-specific epigenomic annotations enriched for SLE genetic associations, as determined by stratified LD score regression. The available annotations are listed here and are drawn from the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA). The plots display p-value (y-axis) and fold enrichment (x-axis) for global enrichment of SLE genetic associations within regions annotated as accessible chromatin, binding sites, enhancers, or promoters. Mouse over the plots to see tissue specificity.
